questions.solution:
Let, $y = \left|{P}^{- 1}AP - 2I\right|$

$⇒ y = \left|{P}^{- 1}AP - 2{P}^{- 1}P\right|$

$⇒ y = \left|\left({P}^{- 1}I\right) ( A - 2I ) P\right|$

$⇒ y = \left|{P}^{- 1}I\right| | A - 2I | | P |$

We know that, $\left|A\right| = 1\left|{A}^{- 1}\right|$.

$⇒ y = | A - 2I |$

$⇒ y = \left|\begin{cases}2 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 2 \\ 6 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 11 \\ 3 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } 2\end{cases}\right| - \left|\begin{cases}2 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 0 \\ 0 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 0 \\ 0 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 2\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ y = \left|\begin{cases}0 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 2 \\ 6 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 11 \\ 3 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } 0\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ y = 0 - \left(0 - 33\right) + 2\left(18 - 0\right)$

$⇒ y = 69$

Now, prime factor of $69$ is $3$ and $23$.

So, sum $= 26$

questions.solution:
Let $M = \left({P}^{- 1}AP - I\right)2$

$= \left({P}^{- 1}AP\right)2 - 2{P}^{- 1}AP + I$

$= {P}^{- 1}{A}^{2}P - 2{P}^{- 1}AP + I\left(∵ \left({P}^{- 1}AP\right)2 = \left({P}^{- 1}AP\right)\left({P}^{- 1}AP\right)\right)$

Multiplying with $P$ on both sides

$⇒ PM = {A}^{2}P - 2AP + P$

$= \left({A}^{2} - 2A . I + {I}^{2}\right)P$

$⇒ Det \left(PM\right) = Det \left(\left(A - I\right)2 \times P\right)$

$⇒ Det \left(PM\right) = Det \left(A - I\right)2 \times Det \left(P\right)$

$⇒ DetM = \left(Det\left(A - I\right)\right)2$

Now $A - I = \left[\begin{cases}1 \text{ and } 7 \text{ and } {w}^{2} \\ - 1 \text{ and } - w - 1 \text{ and } 1 \\ 0 \text{ and } - w \text{ and } - w\end{cases}\right]$

$Det \left(A - I\right) = \left({w}^{2} + w + w\right) + 7\left(- w\right) + {w}^{3} = - 6w$

$Det \left(\left(A - I\right)\right)2 = 36{w}^{2}$

$⇒ \alpha = 36$

questions.solution:
Given that the vectors are coplanar.

That means the determinant is equal to zero.

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 1 \\ 1 \text{ and } b \text{ and } 1 \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } c\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ {R}_{1} \to {R}_{1} – {R}_{2}$ and ${R}_{2} \to {R}_{2} – {R}_{3}$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a - 1 \text{ and } 1 - b \text{ and } 0 \\ 0 \text{ and } b - 1 \text{ and } 1 - c \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } c\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expand the determinant along ${C}_{1}$.

$⇒ ( a - 1 ) [ c ( b - 1 ) - ( 1 - c ) ] + 1 [ ( 1 - b ) ( 1 - c ) ] = 0$

$⇒ c ( a - 1 ) ( b - 1 ) - ( a - 1 ) ( 1 - c ) + ( 1 - b ) ( 1 - c ) = 0$

$⇒ c ( 1 - a ) ( 1 - b ) + ( 1 - a ) ( 1 - c ) + ( 1 - b ) ( 1 - c ) + \left(1 - a\right)\left(1 - b\right)\left(1 - c\right) = \left(1 - a\right)\left(1 - b\right)\left(1 - c\right)$

$⇒ ( 1 - a ) ( 1 - b ) + ( 1 - a ) ( 1 - c ) + ( 1 - b ) ( 1 - c ) = \left(1 - a\right)\left(1 - b\right)\left(1 - c\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{1 - a} + \dfrac{1}{1 - b} + \dfrac{1}{1 - c} = 1$

Hence this is the required option.

questions.question:
Let $p$ and $p + 2$ be prime numbers and let
$\Delta = \left|\begin{cases}p ! \text{ and } \left(p + 1\right) ! \text{ and } \left(p + 2\right) ! \\ \left(p + 1\right) ! \text{ and } \left(p + 2\right) ! \text{ and } \left(p + 3\right) ! \\ \left(p + 2\right) ! \text{ and } \left(p + 3\right) ! \text{ and } \left(p + 4\right) !\end{cases}\right|$
Then the sum of the maximum values of $\alpha$ and $\beta$, such that ${p}^{α}$ and $\left(p + 2\right)\beta$ divide $\Delta$, is _______.
questions.solution:
Given,

$\Delta = \left|\begin{cases}P ! \text{ and } \left(P + 1\right) ! \text{ and } \left(P + 2\right) ! \\ \left(P + 1\right) ! \text{ and } \left(P + 2\right) ! \text{ and } \left(P + 3\right) ! \\ \left(P + 2\right) ! \text{ and } \left(P + 3\right) ! \text{ and } \left(P + 4\right) !\end{cases}\right|$

Now using the factorial concept and taking common terms we get,

$⇒ \Delta = P ! \left(P + 1\right) ! \left(P + 2\right) ! \left|\begin{cases}1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 1 \\ P + 1 \text{ and } P + 2 \text{ and } P + 3 \\ \left(P + 2\right)\left(P + 1\right) \text{ and } \left(P + 3\right)\left(P + 2\right) \text{ and } \left(P + 4\right)\left(P + 3\right)\end{cases}\right|$

Now on solving determinant we get, $\left|\begin{cases}1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 1 \\ P + 1 \text{ and } P + 2 \text{ and } P + 3 \\ \left(P + 2\right)\left(P + 1\right) \text{ and } \left(P + 3\right)\left(P + 2\right) \text{ and } \left(P + 4\right)\left(P + 3\right)\end{cases}\right|$

Using operation ${C}_{1} \to {C}_{1} - {C}_{2} \text{ and } {C}_{2} \to {C}_{2} - {C}_{3}$

$\left|\begin{cases}0 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 1 \\ - 1 \text{ and } - 1 \text{ and } P + 3 \\ - 2P - 4 \text{ and } - 2P - 6 \text{ and } \left(P + 4\right)\left(P + 3\right)\end{cases}\right|$

$= 2P + 6 - \left(2P + 4\right) = 2$

Now putting the value of determinant we get,

$⇒ \Delta = 2P ! \left(P + 1\right) ! \left(P + 2\right) !$

$⇒ \Delta = 2{P}^{3}\left(P - 1\right) ! \left(P + 1\right)\left(P - 1\right) ! \left(P + 2\right)\left(P + 1\right)\left(P - 1\right) !$

Which is divisible by ${P}^{α}$ and $\left(P + 2\right)\beta$

So, $\alpha = 3, \beta = 1$

I: If $\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & \cos \alpha & \cos \beta \\ \cos \alpha & 1 & \cos \gamma \\ \cos \beta & \cos \gamma & 1\end{array}\right|=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}0 & \cos \alpha & \cos \beta \\ \cos \alpha & 0 & \cos \gamma \\ \cos \beta & \cos \gamma & 0\end{array}\right|$, then $\cos ^{2} \alpha+\cos ^{2} \beta+\cos ^{2} \gamma=\frac{3}{2}$, and
II : If $\left|\begin{array}{ccc}x^{2}+x & x+1 & x-2 \\ 2 x^{2}+3 x-1 & 3 x & 3 x-3 \\ x^{2}+2 x+3 & 2 x-1 & 2 x-1\end{array}\right|=\mathrm{p} x+\mathrm{q}$, then $\mathrm{p}^{2}=196 \mathrm{q}^{2}$,
questions.solution:
Statement I: Let $D_1 = \begin{vmatrix} 1 \text{ and } \cos\alpha \text{ and } \cos\beta \\ \cos\alpha \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } \cos\gamma \\ \cos\beta \text{ and } \cos\gamma \text{ and } 1 \end{vmatrix} = 1 - \cos^2\alpha - \cos^2\beta - \cos^2\gamma + 2\cos\alpha\cos\beta\cos\gamma$.
$D_2 = \begin{vmatrix} 0 \text{ and } \cos\alpha \text{ and } \cos\beta \\ \cos\alpha \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } \cos\gamma \\ \cos\beta \text{ and } \cos\gamma \text{ and } 0 \end{vmatrix} = 2\cos\alpha\cos\beta\cos\gamma$.
$D_1 = D_2 \Rightarrow 1 - \cos^2\alpha - \cos^2\beta - \cos^2\gamma = 0 \Rightarrow \cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1 \neq \frac{3}{2}$. Statement I is false.
Statement II: Evaluate by substituting $x = 0$: determinant $= -12$, so $q = -12$.
At $x = 1$: determinant $= 12$, so $p + q = 12 \Rightarrow p = 24$.
$p^2 = 576$ and $196q^2 = 196 \times 144 = 28224$. Since $p^2 \neq 196q^2$, Statement II is false.
Both statements are false.

questions.solution:
Given, $f\left(x\right) = \left|\begin{cases}a \text{ and } - 1 \text{ and } 0 \\ ax \text{ and } a \text{ and } - 1 \\ a{x}^{2} \text{ and } ax \text{ and } a\end{cases}\right|$

$f\left(x\right) = a\left|\begin{cases}1 \text{ and } - 1 \text{ and } 0 \\ x \text{ and } a \text{ and } - 1 \\ {x}^{2} \text{ and } ax \text{ and } a\end{cases}\right|$

$= a\left[1\left({a}^{2} + ax\right) + 1\left(ax + {x}^{2}\right)\right]$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = a\left(x + a\right)2$

Now differentiating the function w.r.t $x$

We get, ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 2a\left(x + a\right)$

Given, $2{f}^{'}\left(10\right) - {f}^{'}\left(5\right) + 100 = 0$

$⇒ 2 \times 2a\left(10 + a\right) - 2a\left(5 + a\right) + 100 = 0$

$⇒ 40a + 4{a}^{2} - 10a - 2{a}^{2} + 100 = 0$

$2{a}^{2} + 30a + 100 = 0$

$⇒ {a}^{2} + 15a + 50 = 0$

$\left(a + 10\right)\left(a + 5\right) = 0$

$a = - 10$ or $a = - 5$

Required $= \left(- 10\right)2 + \left(- 5\right)2 = 125$

questions.question:
If $f: \mathbf{N} \rightarrow \mathbf{Z}$ is defined by
$f(n) = \begin{vmatrix} n \text{ and } -1 \text{ and } -5 \\ -2n^2 \text{ and } 3(2k+1) \text{ and } 2k+1 \\ -3n^3 \text{ and } 3k(2k+1) \text{ and } 3k(k+2)+1 \end{vmatrix}$, $k \in \mathbf{N}$,
and $\sum_{n=1}^{k} f(n) = 98$, then $k$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let $S = \displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{k} f(n)$, where
$f(n) = \begin{vmatrix} n \text{ and } -1 \text{ and } -5 \\ -2n^2 \text{ and } 3(2k+1) \text{ and } 2k+1 \\ -3n^3 \text{ and } 3k(2k+1) \text{ and } 3k(k+2)+1 \end{vmatrix}$

Since only the first column depends on $n$, the summation can be taken inside that column:
$S = \begin{vmatrix} \displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{k} n \text{ and } -1 \text{ and } -5 \\ \displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{k} (-2n^2) \text{ and } 3(2k+1) \text{ and } 2k+1 \\ \displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{k} (-3n^3) \text{ and } 3k(2k+1) \text{ and } 3k(k+2)+1 \end{vmatrix}$

Using standard summation formulas:
$\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{k} n = \dfrac{k(k+1)}{2}$
$\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{k} (-2n^2) = -\dfrac{k(k+1)(2k+1)}{3}$
$\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{k} (-3n^3) = -\dfrac{3k^2(k+1)^2}{4}$

Substituting:

Now using the operation, equation $\left(1\right) \times 4 - \left(2\right)$ we get,

Now using the operation, equation $\left(2\right) \times 2 - \left(3\right)$ we get,

questions.solution:
For the given system of homogeneous linear equations to have a non-trivial solution, the determinant of the coefficient matrix must be zero.

$\begin{vmatrix} \cos 3\theta \text{ and } -8 \text{ and } -12 \\ \cos 2\theta \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } 3 \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 3 \end{vmatrix} = 0$

Expanding the determinant along the first row:

$\cos 3\theta (9 - 3) - (-8)(3\cos 2\theta - 3) + (-12)(\cos 2\theta - 3) = 0$

$6\cos 3\theta + 24\cos 2\theta - 24 - 12\cos 2\theta + 36 = 0$

$6\cos 3\theta + 12\cos 2\theta + 12 = 0$

Dividing by $6$, we get:

$\cos 3\theta + 2\cos 2\theta + 2 = 0$

Using the multiple angle formulas $\cos 3\theta = 4\cos^3 \theta - 3\cos \theta$ and $\cos 2\theta = 2\cos^2 \theta - 1$, we substitute these into the equation:

$(4\cos^3 \theta - 3\cos \theta) + 2(2\cos^2 \theta - 1) + 2 = 0$

$4\cos^3 \theta + 4\cos^2 \theta - 3\cos \theta = 0$

$\cos \theta (4\cos^2 \theta + 4\cos \theta - 3) = 0$

$\cos \theta (2\cos \theta - 1)(2\cos \theta + 3) = 0$

$\sum \theta = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) + \left(\dfrac{\pi}{3} + \dfrac{5\pi}{3}\right) = 2\pi + 2\pi = 4\pi$
